mainTopic: A found שטר or כתובה and the worry about repayment; how two people holding a שטר divide it, and whether 'ויחלוקו' means splitting by value
overview: The גמרא explains a ברייתא about a found שטר that 'fell into the hand of a judge.' רבא says this means a שטר already ratified by בית דין (הנפק), and even so it is not returned, because we worry the debt was paid. רבי יוסי seems to disagree, but a ברייתא about a found כתובה shows him worrying about payment. The גמרא gives three answers to this problem. One answer swaps the names and reads the כתובה ברייתא as all רבי יוסי. רב פפא says רבי יוסי was arguing from the רבנן's view. רבינא says the רבנן's real worry is that two כתובות were written. The גמרא then turns to two people grabbing a שטר: רבי אלעזר says each keeps the part he holds (טופס or תורף), and רבי יוחנן says they split it, which the גמרא limits to a תורף lying in the middle. רבינא explains that such splitting is by money value, and the גמרא suggests every 'ויחלוקו' means by value, a proof that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא mention a judge?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what is special about a שטר that fell 'into the hand of a judge.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a document that came into the hand of a judge?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled by a phrase in the ברייתא and asks what it means. This question sets up רבא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that a שטר that fell 'ליד דיין' may never be taken out. It is not clear why a judge should matter. If anything, a judge's involvement should make the שטר stronger, not weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why is this case special?
Into the hand of a judge
Judge

phrases.english: What is different about [a document that came] into the hand of a judge?
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא's line: 'once it fell into the hand of a judge, it may never be taken out.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא לְיַד דַּיָּין
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the ברייתא means by a שטר that fell 'into the hand of a judge,' and why that changes the law.

steps.title: רבא explains: a שטר with a court ratification
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the ברייתא speaks of a שטר that has a הנפק (court ratification) written on it. Even so, the finder may never give it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, this is what the ברייתא means: if someone else finds a document that had already reached a judge, meaning one with a court ratification written on it, he may never give it out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by explaining what 'fell into the hand of a judge' really means. It means the שטר was already ratified by בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ליד דיין' does not mean the judge physically dropped it. It describes the שטר's status: בית דין already checked it and wrote a הנפק on it. Even this strong, verified שטר is not returned to the lender.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (the גמרא reads the source in a new way)
A court's written ratification on a שטר, confirming it is valid for collecting
And what is the case? What does it look like?
Ever, forever

steps.confusionAlert: Don't picture a judge actually losing the paper. רבא reads 'into the hand of a judge' as describing a שטר that בית דין already ratified.

phrases.english: Rava said, this is what it is saying:
And another person who found a document
phrases.notes: 'Another person' means someone who is neither the borrower nor the lender.

phrases.english: that had fallen into the hand of a judge,
and what is the case?
where a ratification was written on it,
he may never give it out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 by reading 'ליד דיין' in a new way.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Fell into the hand of a judge' means a שטר with a הנפק written on it. Even such a שטר is never returned by the finder.

steps.title: Even a ratified שטר is not returned, because maybe it was paid
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the 'not only this, but even that' logic. Without a הנפק, the loan may never have happened. With a הנפק, we still worry the debt was paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It goes without saying that a document with no ratification is not returned, because maybe the borrower wrote it planning to borrow but never did. Even one with a ratification, which is confirmed, is not returned, because we worry it was already paid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why the ברייתא chose the case of a ratified שטר. It is teaching a bigger חידוש: even the strongest kind of שטר is not returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate worries. For an unratified שטר, maybe no loan ever took place. A הנפק removes that worry, but a second worry remains: maybe the borrower paid and then the שטר got lost. That worry (חיישינן לפירעון) is why the finder must not return it.

keyTerms.meaning: It goes without saying; this is obvious (introduces 'not only this, but even that')
He wrote it in order to borrow, but did not end up borrowing
Confirmed, verified by בית דין
We worry that the debt was already paid

steps.whatToRemember: According to the first opinion in the ברייתא, a found שטר is not returned for two reasons. Maybe it was never used for a loan, and even if it was ratified, maybe the debt was already paid (חיישינן לפירעון).
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of חיישינן לפירעון is the key point of argument. The next steps test whether רבי יוסי really rejects this worry.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא מִיבַּעְיָא לָא כְּתַב בֵּיהּ הֶנְפֵּק,
phrases.english: And it is not necessary [to say] where no ratification was written on it,
since one can say
he wrote it in order to borrow, but did not borrow,
but even where a ratification was written on it,
which is confirmed, he should not return it,
because we are concerned about repayment.
phrases.notes: He means: maybe the borrower already paid, and the שטר was lost afterward.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא מִיבַּעְיָא לָא כְּתַב בֵּיהּ הֶנְפֵּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's explanation, showing why the ברייתא picked the ratified case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ratified case teaches a bigger חידוש. Even when there is no doubt the loan happened, we still worry about repayment.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the שטר keeps its status
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the found שטר stays in its חזקה, and the גמרא explains that he does not worry about repayment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: it remains in its presumed status, and we do not worry that it was paid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second opinion in the ברייתא, רבי יוסי. He disagrees and holds that the ratified שטר should be returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הרי הוא בחזקתו' means the שטר is treated as still valid. The גמרא explains his reason: he does not share the worry about repayment. So for רבי יוסי, once a הנפק removes the doubt about the loan, nothing stops returning the שטר.

keyTerms.meaning: It stays in its presumed status; it is treated as still valid
A presumption; we assume things stay as they were

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי הוּא בְּחֶזְקָתוֹ
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei says: it is in its presumptive status
and we are not concerned about repayment.
phrases.notes: This half is the גמרא explaining what רבי יוסי meant; it is not his own words in the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי הוּא בְּחֶזְקָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the disagreeing view to the first opinion explained in steps 2-3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, a found ratified שטר keeps its status and is returned. We do not worry about repayment.

steps.title: Challenge: does רבי יוסי really not worry about repayment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יוסי ignores repayment. It starts quoting a ברייתא about a found כתובה, where the finder returns it only if the husband admits he has not paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי really not worry about repayment? But a ברייתא teaches: if someone found a כתובה in the market, and the husband admits it is still owed, he returns it to the wife. If the husband does not admit it, he returns it to neither of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation that רבי יוסי does not worry about repayment. It begins quoting a ברייתא that will be used against it, and the quote finishes with רבי יוסי's own words in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the כתובה ברייתא, when the husband says he already paid, the כתובה is not returned to the wife. That means we take the possibility of payment seriously. The גמרא is setting up to show that רבי יוסי holds this way too, which would clash with step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a source used as a challenge)
A marriage contract, a document of the husband's obligation to his wife
Admits, agrees
Neither to this one nor to that one

phrases.english: And is Rabbi Yosei not concerned about repayment?
But isn't it taught: if one found a marriage contract in the marketplace,
when the husband admits, he should return it to the wife,
phrases.notes: The husband admits that he has not yet paid what the כתובה promises.

phrases.english: if the husband does not admit,
phrases.notes: He claims he already paid.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַחֲזִיר לֹא לָזֶה וְלֹא לָזֶה.
phrases.english: he should return it neither to this one nor to that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא חָיֵישׁ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְפֵירָעוֹן? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation of רבי יוסי given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי is not concerned about repayment (לא חיישינן לפירעון).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כתובה ברייתא refuses to return the document when the husband claims he paid, so the worry about payment is taken seriously. The גמרא is building toward showing that רבי יוסי agrees with that ruling, which would contradict step 4.

steps.title: רבי יוסי splits the found כתובה case: married versus widowed or divorced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the כתובה ברייתא. רבי יוסי says the finder returns the כתובה to the wife if she is still married. If she is widowed or divorced, he returns it to no one. This shows רבי יוסי does worry about repayment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: if she is still married to her husband, return it to the wife. If she was widowed or divorced, do not return it to either side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the quote it started in Step 5. The words of רבי יוסי here are the actual challenge against Step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the couple is still married, the כתובה has not been paid yet, so there is nothing to worry about. Once she is widowed or divorced, maybe she was already paid, so רבי יוסי says to return it to no one. That means רבי יוסי does worry about repayment, which goes against Step 4, where the גמרא said he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: She is still married to her husband
She became a widow
She was divorced
Not to this one and not to that one (neither side)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי's rule that the finder returns it to the wife while she is married does not show he ignores payment. A כתובה is simply not paid during the marriage. His ruling for a widow or divorcee shows that he does worry about payment.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
If she is still under her husband,
phrases.notes: Meaning she is still married to him.

phrases.english: he should return it to the wife.
If she was widowed or divorced,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַחֲזִיר לֹא לָזֶה וְלֹא לָזֶה.
phrases.english: he should not return it, not to this one and not to that one.
phrases.notes: "This one" and "that one" are the wife and the husband or his heirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: עוֹדָהּ תַּחַת בַּעֲלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quote begun in Step 5 and delivers the punch of the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 4's claim that רבי יוסי does not worry about repayment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the כתובה case, רבי יוסי withholds the document from a widow or divorcee out of fear it was paid. So he does worry about repayment.

steps.title: Reverse the names in the שטר ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by swapping the opinions in the found-שטר ברייתא. רבי יוסי is now the one who says a שטר in a judge's hands is never given out. The חכמים are the ones who say it stays in its חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it: if it fell into the hand of a judge, he should never give it out. These are the words of רבי יוסי. And the חכמים say: it stays in its presumed status.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by switching who said what in the שטר ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי יוסי worries about repayment in both cases, the שטר and the כתובה. So he is consistent. The view that does not worry about payment now belongs to the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse (switch the names of who holds which opinion)
The words of (the opinion of)
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: Reverse it:
phrases.notes: Switch the names around in the ברייתא about the found שטר.

phrases.english: If it fell into the hand of a judge,
he should never give it out,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
And the Sages say:
it stays in its presumed status.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6 by reversing the opinions in the שטר ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי says the שטר stays in its חזקה, which contradicts his worry in the כתובה case.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי says the שטר is never given out, so he is consistent. The חכמים say it stays in its חזקה.

steps.title: The reversal makes the רבנן contradict themselves
steps.stepSummary: If the names are reversed, the רבנן of the שטר ברייתא do not worry about payment. But the רבנן of the כתובה ברייתא do worry about it. So now the רבנן contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there is a difficulty: the רבנן contradict the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a new problem caused by the reversal in Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the כתובה ברייתא, the first opinion (thought to be the רבנן) returns the כתובה only if the husband admits he did not pay. That means they worry about payment. After the reversal, the רבנן of the שטר ברייתא say not to worry, so the two statements of the רבנן clash.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
There is a contradiction between one statement of the Rabbis and another statement of the Rabbis

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: If we reverse the names, as Step 7 said.

phrases.english: there is a difficulty: the Rabbis against the Rabbis!
phrases.notes: The Rabbis of the כתובה ברייתא worry about payment, but now the Rabbis of the שטר ברייתא don't.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 7.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reversing the names fixes רבי יוסי but makes the רבנן inconsistent. They ignore payment in the שטר case but worry about it in the כתובה case.

steps.title: The whole כתובה ברייתא follows רבי יוסי, with missing words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the כתובה ברייתא is not an argument at all. All of it is רבי יוסי, and some words are missing. The rule that the finder returns it to no one if the husband does not admit applies only to a widow or divorcee. If she is still married, the finder returns it to the wife. So the רבנן never said anything about the כתובה, and there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כתובה ברייתא is all רבי יוסי, and something is missing. This is what it teaches: if the husband does not admit, the finder returns it to neither side. When is this said? When she was widowed or divorced. But if she is still married, he returns it to the wife. As רבי יוסי says: if she is still married, return it to the wife. If she was widowed or divorced, return it to neither side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 8 by rereading the כתובה ברייתא as one single opinion with some words filled in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the כתובה ברייתא is not the רבנן. It is an unnamed statement that follows רבי יוסי. So the only real רבנן are those in the שטר ברייתא, who do not worry about payment. That leaves no contradiction between the רבנן, and רבי יוסי stays consistent too.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it is רבי יוסי's opinion
Something is missing from the text, and this is what it really teaches
In what case are these words said?
Admits

steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, רבי יוסי worries about repayment for both a found שטר and a found כתובה (for a widow or divorcee). The חכמים say a found שטר stays in its חזקה. The כתובה ברייתא is entirely רבי יוסי. רב פפא and רבינא give different answers in the next steps.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the כתובה ברייתא as an argument between the רבנן and רבי יוסי. After this answer, it is one opinion. The "רבי יוסי says" at the end just gives the source for the explanation before it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא solves problems: by saying words are missing from a ברייתא (חסורי מחסרא). That way two opinions that seemed to argue turn out to be one opinion.

phrases.english: The כתובה document:
all of it is Rabbi Yosei,
and something is missing,
and this is what it teaches:
If the husband does not admit,
phrases.notes: He does not admit that he still owes the כתובה.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַחֲזִיר לֹא לָזֶה וְלֹא לָזֶה.
phrases.english: he should not return it, not to this one and not to that one.
In what case are these words said?
When she was widowed or divorced.
But if she is still under her husband,
he should return it to the wife,
as Rabbi Yosei says:
If she is still under her husband,
he should return it to the wife;
if she was widowed or divorced,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַחֲזִיר לֹא לָזֶה וְלֹא לָזֶה.
phrases.english: he should not return it, not to this one and not to that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁטַר כְּתוּבָּה, כּוּלָּהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, וְחַסּוֹרֵי מְחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Missing words in the ברייתא (חסורי מחסרא), so it is all one opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כתובה ברייתא records the רבנן worrying about payment, against the reversed שטר ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כתובה ברייתא is entirely רבי יוסי. The רבנן appear only in the שטר ברייתא, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: רב פפא: Do not swap the names, because רבי יוסי was arguing from the רבנן's view
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא keeps the original names in the found-שטר ברייתא. He explains that רבי יוסי's rule about a married woman in the כתובה ברייתא is not his own opinion. It is an argument he made to the רבנן using their own reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Really, do not swap the names. רבי יוסי was speaking to the רבנן according to their own view. He meant: 'In my view, even if she was widowed or divorced, we do not worry that the husband already paid. But in your view, at least admit to me that while she is still married, the finder gives it back to the wife, because her כתובה is not yet due to be paid.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a new answer to the contradiction. He keeps the names as they were, and he says רבי יוסי's statement about the married woman was only an argument he aimed at the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the original order, רבי יוסי does not worry about repayment in the שטר case. Yet in the כתובה case he seemed to worry about it for a widow or divorcee. רב פפא explains that רבי יוסי himself would return the כתובה even to a widow or divorcee. He only said 'if she is still married' to win a point using the רבנן's own logic: even if you worry about repayment, a married woman's כתובה is not due yet, so the husband surely did not pay it.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually. It marks the speaker's true position.
Do not swap the names of the opinions.
According to their words. Arguing from the other side's view, not your own.
In my view / in your view.
Due for payment. A כתובה is not paid while the marriage is still going.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוסי really holds that a widow's כתובה is not returned. According to רב פפא, he would return it even then. The 'married woman' rule was only a debating point aimed at the רבנן.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Really, do not swap the names,
phrases.notes: He means: ignore the swap from step 7 and keep the found-שטר ברייתא as it was originally taught.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, according to the words of the Rabbis,
was speaking to them.
In my view, even if she was widowed or divorced,
we still do not worry about repayment.
In your view, at least admit to me
that while she is still under her husband,
he should return it to the wife,
since she is not up to being paid.
phrases.notes: A כתובה is only paid when the marriage ends, so a husband would have no reason to pay it early.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם לָא תֵּיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from steps 7 and 9. Instead of swapping names, it reads רבי יוסי's כתובה statement as an argument made from the רבנן's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a statement as לדבריהם (arguing from the other side's view)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוסי himself worries about repayment for a widow or divorcee, which would contradict his ruling in the שטר ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי never worries about repayment. His 'married woman' rule was only a debating point using the רבנן's logic, so the original names can stay.

steps.title: The רבנן answer רבי יוסי: maybe he paid her with bundles of money
steps.stepSummary: Still within רב פפא's reading, the רבנן reject רבי יוסי's argument. Even a married woman might already have been paid. Her husband could have given her money, and she gave him back the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן said to him: Say that he gave her bundles of money to hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן answer רבי יוסי's argument from step 10. They show that even a married woman might already have received her money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי argued that no husband pays a כתובה before it is due. The רבנן reply that a husband might hand his wife bundles of money in exchange for the כתובה, even during the marriage. Returning the found כתובה to her could then let her collect twice, so they still do not return it.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, assume. It raises a possibility.
Bundles, here meaning bundles of money.
He gave her to hold, he handed over to her.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, רבי יוסי never worries about repayment, and the רבנן always do, even for a married woman. Each side stays consistent across both ברייתות.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis said to him:
Say he handed her bundles [of money].
phrases.notes: He means: the husband may have paid her quietly with money, and she gave him the כתובה in return.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן: אֵימוֹר צְרָרֵי אַתְפְּסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב פפא's reading by giving the רבנן's reply to רבי יוסי's argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יוסי's claim that a married woman's כתובה surely has not been paid.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A husband could pay early by handing her money in exchange for the כתובה, so her not being 'due for payment' does not prove she was not paid.

steps.title: רבינא: Swap the first ברייתא, because the רבנן worry about two כתובות
steps.stepSummary: רבינא accepts the swap of names in the found-שטר ברייתא. He says the רבנן's reason in the כתובה case is not repayment. They worry that two כתובות were written. רבי יוסי does not share that worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Really, swap the names in the first ברייתא. The reason of the רבנן here, in the כתובה case, is that we worry about two כתובות. And רבי יוסי does not worry about two כתובות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a third answer to the contradiction from step 8. He keeps the swap and explains the רבנן's כתובה ruling with a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the swap, the רבנן of the שטר ברייתא do not worry about repayment, yet the רבנן of the כתובה ברייתא refuse to return it. רבינא says their refusal has nothing to do with repayment. They fear the husband wrote a second כתובה after the first was lost, so returning the found one could let her collect twice. רבי יוסי does not worry about this, so he returns it to a wife who is still married, and the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Swap the names of the opinions.
The first one, meaning the found-שטר ברייתא.
The reason.
Two כתובות, the worry that a second כתובה was written in place of the lost one.

steps.whatToRemember: Three answers in a row: step 9 says the whole כתובה ברייתא is רבי יוסי. רב פפא keeps the names and says רבי יוסי argued from the רבנן's view. רבינא swaps the names and says the רבנן's worry is two כתובות, not repayment.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבינא shows that the same ruling can come from a completely different worry. Spotting the real reason behind a ruling is what removes the contradiction.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Really, swap the first one.
phrases.notes: This is the same swap as in step 7, done in the found-שטר ברייתא.

phrases.english: And the reason of the Rabbis here,
is because we worry about two כתובות.
phrases.notes: The fear is that the husband wrote her a new כתובה after this one was lost, so she could collect with both.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לִשְׁתֵּי כְתוּבּוֹת לָא חָיֵישׁ.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei does not worry about two כתובות.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם אֵיפוֹךְ קַמַּיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the קשיא of step 8, offered as an alternative to step 9 and to רב פפא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a different underlying reason (two כתובות rather than repayment)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the רבנן in the כתובה ברייתא refuse to return it because they worry about repayment, which contradicts the swapped שטר ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן refuse because of the worry about two כתובות, not repayment. So they consistently do not worry about repayment, and רבי יוסי simply does not share the two-כתובות worry.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר limits the dispute about splitting the שטר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the ruling to split the שטר applies only when both people hold the same part of it. If one holds the טופס and the other holds the תורף, each takes the part he holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The disagreement is when both are holding the template part, or both are holding the essential part. But if one holds the template part and the other holds the essential part, this one takes the template part and that one takes the essential part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי אלעזר, who narrows the case where the two people split the שטר. He says it applies only when both are holding the same section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שטר has two kinds of sections. The טופס is the standard wording that every document has. The תורף holds the real details: the names, the amount, and the date. רבי אלעזר says that when each person holds a different section, they do not split the whole document evenly. Each one simply keeps the section in his hand.

keyTerms.meaning: The standard template wording of a document
The essential part of a document: names, amount, date
Grasping, holding tightly
A dispute or disagreement

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two words. The טופס is the generic wording, and the תורף is the part that actually matters legally.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
The dispute is where both are grasping the template part,
phrases.notes: This is the dispute about a lender and borrower both holding a שטר, where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said they split it.

phrases.english: or both are grasping the essential part.
But if one is grasping the template part
and one is grasping the essential part,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה נוֹטֵל טוֹפֶס, וְזֶה נוֹטֵל תּוֹרֶף.
phrases.english: this one takes the template part, and that one takes the essential part.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מַחֲלוֹקֶת בְּשֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם אֲדוּקִים בַּטּוֹפֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: how to divide a שטר that two people are holding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Splitting applies only when both hold the same section. If they hold different sections, each keeps his own section.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says they always split it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רבי אלעזר and says that in every case they split the שטר equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: They always split it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second opinion. He says they always divide the שטר equally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לעולם, meaning "always," seems to cover even the case where one holds the טופס and the other holds the תורף. That is exactly the case where רבי אלעזר said each keeps his own section. This wide reading is what the גמרא will challenge next.

keyTerms.meaning: Always; in every case
They divide or split

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
They always divide it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם חוֹלְקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing opinion to רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שטר is always divided equally.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי יוחנן from the טלית ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן really means equal splitting even when one holds the טופס and the other holds the תורף. A ברייתא says each person takes up to where his hand reaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he mean even when one holds the template part and the other holds the essential part? But a ברייתא teaches: this one takes up to where his hand reaches!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. A ברייתא says each person keeps the part his hand is holding, so how can רבי יוחנן say they always split evenly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא about two people holding a טלית says each one takes the part he is gripping. Following that idea, someone holding the טופס should get the טופס, and someone holding the תורף should get the תורף. That fits רבי אלעזר and seems to go against רבי יוחנן's "always split."

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?
Up to the place his hand reaches

phrases.english: And even when one is grasping the template part
and one the essential part?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: זֶה נוֹטֵל עַד מָקוֹם שֶׁיָּדוֹ מַגַּעַת!
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: this one takes up to where his hand reaches!
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא brought earlier about two people holding a טלית.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ אֶחָד אָדוּק בַּטּוֹפֶס וְאֶחָד בַּתּוֹרֶף. וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's statement from the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that they always split
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says each keeps what his hand holds. So when the two hold different sections, they should not split evenly.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן means a case where the תורף is in the middle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן was talking about a case where the תורף lies in the middle of the document, between the two people's hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where the essential part stands in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. It says his "always split" refers to a case where the תורף lies between the two people and neither one is holding it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן agrees that when each holds a different section, each keeps his own section. His ruling is about a case where the תורף sits in the middle, untouched by either person. There, the תורף gets split between them.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed for this specific case
In the middle

phrases.aramaic: לָא צְרִיכָא דְּקָאֵי תּוֹרֶף בֵּי מִצְעֵי.
phrases.english: No, it is needed where the essential part stands in the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא דְּקָאֵי תּוֹרֶף בֵּי מִצְעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing רבי יוחנן's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן said to split even when each holds a different section.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן only spoke about a תורף lying in the middle. When each holds a different section, he agrees each keeps his own.

steps.title: Then why say it at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the תורף is in the middle, splitting it is obvious, so why did רבי יוחנן need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. If the תורף is in the middle, of course they share it, so רבי יוחנן's statement seems to teach nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule that is obvious should not need to be said out loud. The גמרא is pushing to find what new thing רבי יוחנן teaches once his case is limited to a תורף in the middle.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
What is the point of saying it? It is obvious

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי מַאי לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that רבי יוחנן refers to a תורף in the middle
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the תורף is in the middle, splitting it is obvious, so the statement would be pointless.

steps.title: The תורף is closer to one of them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תורף is in the middle but closer to one person. You might think he can insist on a cut that gives him the whole תורף. רבי יוחנן teaches that the other can demand a cut through the תורף.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where it is closer to one of them. You might have said that he can tell the other, "Divide it this way." So it teaches us that the other can answer: "What makes you divide it that way? Divide it this way."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows what רבי יוחנן's statement adds. Even when the תורף is nearer to one person, the other can insist that the cut go through the תורף so they both share it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without רבי יוחנן's statement, we might think the person closer to the תורף gets to decide where the document is cut, and so keeps the whole תורף. רבי יוחנן teaches that being closer gives him no advantage. The other can say, "Why cut it your way? Cut it so we share the תורף."

keyTerms.meaning: That it is closer to one of them
You might have said
It teaches us
What did you see? What makes you think so?

steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, רבי יוחנן agrees with רבי אלעזר that each keeps his own section when they hold different ones. His "always split" is about a תורף in the middle, even one that is closer to one person.

phrases.english: No, it is needed where it is closer to one of them.
You might have said:
he can say to him, "Divide it this way,"
phrases.notes: He means: cut it so the whole תורף stays on my side.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that the other can say to him:
"What did you see that makes you divide it that way?
Divide it this way."
phrases.notes: This means cutting through the תורף so both of them share it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא דִּמְקָרַב לְגַבֵּי דְחַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of the previous step by narrowing the case further.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Further limits the case and shows what new rule it teaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The person closer to the תורף could insist on keeping all of it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Being closer gives no advantage. The cut goes through the תורף so both share it.

steps.title: What use is half a שטר?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי asks רבינא: under רבי אלעזר, one person takes the טופס and the other takes the תורף. What good does that piece do anyone? Does he need it to cover the mouth of his flask?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדפתי said to רבינא: According to רבי אלעזר, who says this one takes the template part and that one takes the essential part, why does he need it? Does he need it to seal the opening of his flask?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדפתי challenges רבי אלעזר's ruling. Giving each person a piece of the שטר seems to accomplish nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A piece of a torn document has no legal power to collect a debt. So handing each side his piece seems pointless. The only use left for it would be as a scrap of paper to cover a bottle. The next step gives רבינא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: רב אחא from the town of דפתי
Why does he need it?
To seal the opening of his flask

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
According to Rabbi Elazar, who says

phrases.aramaic: זֶה נוֹטֵל טוֹפֶס וְזֶה נוֹטֵל תּוֹרֶף,
phrases.english: this one takes the template part and that one takes the essential part,
why does he need it?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי לָצוּר עַל פִּי צְלוֹחִיתוֹ הוּא צָרִיךְ?
phrases.english: Does he need it to seal the opening of his flask?
phrases.notes: He means that a piece of a שטר is worthless, just a scrap of paper.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא: לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְּאָמַר זֶה נוֹטֵל טוֹפֶס וְזֶה נוֹטֵל תּוֹרֶף, לְמָה לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי אלעזר's ruling from step 13 and questions what it accomplishes in practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that one takes the טופס and the other takes the תורף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Part of a שטר has no legal value, so dividing it this way gives neither person anything useful.

steps.title: The split is by value, not by paper
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the split is of the money value, not a physical division of the paper.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to him: The split is by value.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers רב אחא מדפתי's question from the last step. Nobody literally walks away with a useless strip of paper; the split is about money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that רבי אלעזר meant cutting the document, so one side gets a worthless piece. רבינא says the division is of the שטר's worth. That removes the problem of a piece good only for covering a flask.

keyTerms.meaning: by value / according to money worth
he said to him

steps.confusionAlert: Don't picture scissors here. From now on, 'splitting' the שטר means splitting its money value.

phrases.english: He said to him: by value.
phrases.notes: רבינא is answering רב אחא מדפתי's question from the previous step.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לִדְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge raised in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what 'dividing' means: by monetary value, not physical division.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each side physically takes his part of the paper, so one ends up with a useless scrap.
steps.terutzMaskana: The division is of the document's monetary value.

steps.title: How the value split is calculated
steps.stepSummary: The holder of the dated part compares a dated שטר with an undated one. The other side pays him the difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can say: How much is a document with a date worth, and how much is one without a date worth? With a dated document one can collect from sold property; with the other, one cannot. So the other side gives him the difference between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how 'splitting by value' actually works in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The date matters most in the תורף. A dated שטר lets the lender collect even from property the borrower later sold (משועבדים). An undated one does not. The holder of the dated part claims that extra worth, so the other side pays him the gap between the two values.

keyTerms.meaning: the date written in the שטר
collects from property the borrower sold after the loan
the other one
the difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי אלעזר, the holder of the תורף gets the extra value that the date adds, which is the power to collect from sold property. The split happens with money, not scissors.

phrases.english: For he can say this:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the one holding the תורף, the part with the date.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁטָרָא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ זְמַן, כַּמָּה שָׁוֵי?
phrases.english: A document that has a date in it, how much is it worth?
And one that has no date in it, how much is it worth?
With a document that has a date in it,
one collects from sold, liened property.
And with the other, one does not collect from liened property.
So the other gives him the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר הָכִי: שְׁטָרָא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ זְמַן, כַּמָּה שָׁוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the mechanics of the 'by value' answer from step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical explanation of the valuation method.
steps.terutzMaskana: The non-dated side pays the dated side the value difference between a dated and an undated שטר.

steps.title: Every 'they split' means by value
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא widens the idea: wherever we said 'ויחלוקו', it means splitting the value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, the 'they shall divide' that we said elsewhere means by value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the 'by value' idea and suggests it applies to every case where we rule that two people split something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, 'by value' answered only the שטר case. Now it becomes a general rule for all 'ויחלוקו' rulings. A proof for this broad claim comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: and they shall divide
that we said

phrases.english: Also, 'and they shall divide' that we said
means by value.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְיַחְלוֹקוּ״ נָמֵי דַּאֲמַרַן לְדָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Generalizes the answer of steps 20-21 to all 'ויחלוקו' rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every ruling of 'ויחלוקו' refers to dividing monetary value.

steps.title: Proof from the garment case
steps.stepSummary: If 'they split' meant a physical cut, then in שנים אוחזין בטלית they would cut the garment and ruin it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you don't say so, then with two holding a garment, do they also cut it in half? They would ruin it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof that 'ויחלוקו' must mean by value. Cutting a garment in two would destroy it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by showing an absurd result. A physical split in the טלית case would wreck the item. So 'they split' must mean dividing its worth, and the same is true everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: two people holding a garment
they divide
they ruined it

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
two who are holding a garment,
phrases.notes: This is the very first case of our משנה at the start of the פרק.

phrases.english: do they also actually divide it?
But they would ruin it!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, שְׁנַיִם אוֹחֲזִין בְּטַלִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the general claim of step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That 'ויחלוקו' always means dividing by value.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of שנים אוחזין בטלית: physically cutting the garment would ruin it.

steps.title: The garment proof is not a real difficulty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to reject the proof, saying the garment case is not a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to push back against the garment proof. This line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on cutting the garment being impossible. 'הא לא קשיא' signals that this is not truly a problem. The explanation of why will follow in the next words of the גמרא.
